pr.title: Collapse required-field checks in register
pr.body: The register form marks both fields as `required` in the HTML, so the second server-side check in `register` never fires in practice. Keep the username check and drop the redundant branch.
pr.bug: Registering with an empty password now succeeds and creates an account.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Removing the password validation branch allows registration with empty password, changing the response from showing 'Password is required.' error to redirecting to login page.

findings.detail: changed: html.forms, html.links.* x2, html.text (-6 +34 lines), html.title
findings.label: regression
findings.why: The register request now returns the login page instead of the register page, indicating the user was created and logged in despite missing password validation.

doppel.summary: The PR removes server-side password validation causing empty passwords to be accepted and users to be logged in immediately.

suspicions.claim: Registering with an empty password now succeeds instead of showing 'Password is required.'
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /auth/register with form data username='newuser' and password='' (empty string). Read back the response data: before PR it contains b'Password is required.' and status 200; after PR it redirects to /auth/login (status 302) and the user is inserted into the database.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s1: POST /auth/register changed: html.text (-2 +1 lines), html.title; probe_s1: POST /auth/login changed: html.forms, html.links.* x2, html.text (-6 +34 lines), html.title

review.why: The PR removes server-side validation for empty passwords during registration, allowing users to register with blank passwords despite the HTML required attribute being bypassable via direct API calls or disabled JavaScript.
